data.rationale:
DISCOVERY: We already have ML data collection infrastructure capturing:
- 2,421 commits (with diffs, messages)
- 186 sessions (with chat IDs)
- 19 chats (query/response pairs with tools used)

WHAT WE LEARN by communicating:
1. With OURSELVES: Decision chains, reasoning patterns, cognitive breakdowns, recovery paths
2. With USERS: What questions matter, what explanations work, what confuses them
3. With SYSTEMS: Tool success/failure rates, common errors, performance patterns

THE GAP: We capture the RAW DATA but don't do LEARNING EXTRACTION. The 'pure form' exists in .git-ml/, but we lack:
1. Cognitive state markers (confusion, breakthrough, recovery)
2. Error pattern analysis (what approaches failed and why)
3. Pattern extraction (recurring solutions across sessions)
4. Explicit learning events (I learned X because Y happened)

PROPOSAL: Create 'learning events' - explicit captures of:
- What was learned
- What triggered the learning
- Before/after cognitive state
- Transferable pattern extracted

This would augment (not replace) existing data collection with semantic meaning.
data.title: What we learn and how to capture it in pure form
